 Dated this the 17th day of November, 2025  JUDGMENT
These two Writ Petitions are connected and therefore, I am disposing of these cases by a common judgment.

The prayers in W.P. (C) No.2837 of 2023 are extracted hereunder:
"i) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction directing the respondents 1 to 5 to conduct a detailed enquiry into the complaints evidenced by Ext.P3 to P6 and take immediate steps to cancel the licenses/permission /Consent/NOC issued in favour of the 8 th respondent to run the restaurant under the name Thaal Kitchen forthwith.

ii) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction directing the respondents 1 to 5 to take immediate steps to close down the Restaurant named 'Thaal Kitchen' illegally run by the 8th Respondent without following the food safety norms, health and hygiene standards and waste disposal requirements insisted by respondents 1 to 4.

iii) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction directing the respondents 2 and 4 to ensure strict compliance with Rule 79 of the Kerala Municipality Building Rules 2019 before permitting the 8th respondent to run the restaurant.

iv) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other WP(C) Nos.2837 & 106 OF 2023 2025:KER:87998 appropriate writ, order or direction directing the respondents 1 and 2 to ensure prompt implementation of the directions contained in Ext.P7 forthwith.

v) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction directing the respondents 1 to 4 to consider Ext.P3 to P6 and take stern action against the 8th respondent in running the restaurant under the name and style "Thaal Kitchen" in violation to the statutory requirements.

vi) issue such other and further reliefs as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case;
vii) petitioners may be permitted to dispense with the vernacular documents;
viii) award costs to the petitioners."

is filed challenging Ext.P3 order, and according to the petitioner, the same is passed without issuing a preliminary order.
is filed for a direction to the respondents 1 to 4 to consider Exts.P3 to P6 complaints, and for a direction to implement the directions contained in Ext.P7.

Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners in these Writ Petitions, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Corporation, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Kerala State Pollution Control Board and the learned Government Pleader.
5.
The short point raised by the petitioner in W.P.(C) No.106/2023 is that, Ext.P3 order is passed without issuing a preliminary order.
This Court perused Ext.P3 order.
There is nothing to show that a preliminary order is preceded before passing Ext.P3.

For that simple reason, without going to the merit of the case, Ext.P3 can be set aside, and there can be a direction to the Corporation to proceed in accordance with the law, after issuing a preliminary order and thereafter hearing all the parties, pass appropriate orders in accordance with the law.

Therefore, these Writ Petitions are disposed of in the following manner:
1. Ext.P3 order produced in W.P.(C) No.106/2023 is set aside.

2. The 1st respondent Corporation is directed to issue a provisional order in accordance with Section 406(1) of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, and thereafter give an opportunity of hearing to the petitioners in these cases and pass appropriate order in accordance with the law.
The final order, as directed above, should be passed within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

Sd/-
 P.V.KUNHIKRISHNAN
